question: Article 76 of the Constitution of India provides for:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Attorney General**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Explanation of Article 76:**

 
 
• Article 76 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment and role of the **Attorney General of India**.
 
• The Attorney General is the highest law officer in the country and serves as the chief legal advisor to the Government of India.
 
• They have the right to speak and take part in proceedings of both Houses of Parliament but cannot vote.
 
• The Attorney General is appointed by the President of India and must be qualified to be a judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• The role includes providing legal advice to the government and representing it in important legal matters.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ombudsman:**

 
 
• The Ombudsman, also known as the **Lokpal** or **Lokayukta**, is an anti-corruption authority in India.
 
• It is not mentioned in Article 76 but is established under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.
 
• The Ombudsman investigates allegations of corruption against public officials.
 
 
 
• **Finance Commission Chairman:**
 
 
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body established under **Article 280** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is responsible for recommending the distribution of financial resources between the central and state governments.
 
• The Chairman and members are appointed by the President of India.
 
 
 
• **Election Commissioner:**
 
 
• The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority established under **Article 324**.
 
• It is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India.
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners are appointed by the President of India.
